attempts.summary: Discovered the real topology (node1 has 3 NICs: eth0=shared default net, eth1↔node2, eth2↔node3, both dhcp:false/egress:false private links requiring manual addressing); assigned static IPs and routes so node2/node3 route through node1, opened firewalld on the private NICs, applied a VyOS QoS HTB shaper (1Mbit rate/ceiling) on node1's eth2 egress (the node3-facing interface), and validated with iperf3 that node2→node3 is capped at ~1 Mbit/s while node3→node2 remains unrestricted (~1-20+ Gbit/s). All three nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, with boot-id changes proving actual restarts, and post-restart verification confirmed IP config, routes, firewall zones, VyOS QoS shaping, and the required asymmetric throughput behavior all persisted.
